stage: Initial visual direction — three key screens
note: Raster UI mockups with illustrative workspace data. These do not certify accessibility conformance or implement application behavior.

screens.title: Workspace overview
screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high-resolution, exceptionally polished desktop application screenshot for ProcureAI, a procurement workspace for small and medium businesses. This is an actual flat, full-bleed UI mockup image, NOT code, a website marketing page, an illustration, a laptop/device render, or a presentation collage. Landscape 1920 x 1200 composition, straight-on, one complete screen. Design quality of a mature professional enterprise application. Screen: WORKSPACE OVERVIEW.

SHARED DESIGN SYSTEM, to establish for the whole screen family:
Premium enterprise LIGHT theme. White main workspace, very subtle cool off-white canvas (#F7F8FA), pale gray borders (#DEE4E9), dark slate text (#1D2935), readable secondary text (#526170), restrained dark forest-green primary actions (#285447). No gradients, glow, glassmorphism, saturated color blocks, decorative graphics, emoji, huge rounded cards or ornamental charts. Crisp Inter-like sans serif typography: 28px page title, 16px body, 14px controls and labels, minimum 12px secondary metadata. Consistent 8px spacing grid, 6px border radii, restrained line icons from one family, minimal shadows. Aim for strong accessible contrast, visible labels, text plus icons for statuses, comfortable hit targets. Dense enough to be useful; generous but purposeful whitespace. All text must be crisp, professional and correctly spelled.

APP SHELL:
224px white left sidebar separated by a hairline. Small geometric monogram and wordmark "ProcureAI" at top. Workspace selector "Meridian Works". Navigation with monochrome line icons: Overview (selected with pale green rectangular background), Requests, Suppliers, RFQs, Quotations, Approvals with a small count "2", Purchase orders. Lower section: Activity & agents, AI usage, Settings. Bottom: circular initials "AM", "Ada Morgan", secondary "Procurement manager"; a subtle "Sample workspace" text label.
Top header 64px high: breadcrumb "Workspace / Overview", discreet search input labeled "Search requests, suppliers..." and keyboard hint, notification bell, circular initials AM.

SCREEN CONTENT:
Page header left title "Procurement overview"; smaller description "Keep purchasing moving, from request to approved order." Right a restrained outlined "Export summary" button and solid forest-green "+ New request" button.
Below, four clean inline metrics separated by thin vertical rules, NOT four floating cards: "Open requests  8", "Awaiting approval  2", "Quotes to review  3", "Approved POs  4". Small scope caption "Sample workspace · November 2026". These are sample counts, no fake trends or invented savings percentages.
Main content two unequal columns.
Left 70%: a practical panel titled "Needs your attention", short secondary "The next action on each purchase". Tabs "All tasks" selected, "My requests", "Approvals"; a restrained filter control. A precise readable table:
headers "Request", "Next action", "Owner", "Due", "Amount".
Row1 "PR-014" secondary "20 development laptops"; next action icon plus "Review supplier award"; owner "Ada Morgan"; due "Today"; amount "$18,300".
Row2 "PR-012" secondary "Office workstations"; "Confirm quotation details"; "Daniel Okafor"; "24 Nov"; "$7,200".
Row3 "PR-011" secondary "Meeting room equipment"; "Review PO release"; "Ada Morgan"; "Today"; "$4,850".
Row4 "PR-009" secondary "Warehouse label printers"; "Select suppliers"; "Nina Patel"; "26 Nov"; "$3,600".
Row5 "PR-008" secondary "Ergonomic office chairs"; "Complete requirements"; "Lena Brooks"; "27 Nov"; "$6,000".
Use subtle row separators, alignment, readable prices, no rainbow badges. Highlight only the first next action with a quiet amber text/icon where needed. Bottom small "View all requests" text link.
Below this panel a compact horizontal process summary titled "Purchasing pipeline", with modest labeled segments "Requirements 2", "Sourcing 3", "Review 2", "PO preparation 1", neutral and green tones; make it a small meaningful sample workflow visualization, not a big analytics chart.
Right 30%: "Pending decisions" narrow functional section with two divided approval summaries. First "Supplier award", "20 development laptops", "Atlas Computing · $18,300", "Delivery: 12 days", a forest-green "Review decision" button. Second "PO release", "Meeting room equipment", "$4,850", small "Review PO" link. Under a thin divider: "Recent activity", three concise timestamped lines: "Quotations compared · PR-014 · 12 min ago"; "RFQ exported · PR-009 · 38 min ago"; "PO approved · PO-004 · 1 hr ago".
At bottom right of workspace, a discreet outlined "Procurement copilot" button with one restrained line icon, not a floating neon AI widget.

CONSTRAINTS:
Visually intentional professional enterprise software. No subscription, checkout, payment, invoices, forecasting or enterprise module navigation. No fictional live integrations, no autonomous purchasing claim, no meaningless charts. Do not copy another company's interface. No browser chrome, no outer device frame, no watermark, no explanatory design annotations outside the product screen. Render all content within bounds with precise alignment and unclipped controls.

screens.title: Quotation comparison
screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the reference application screenshot into a NEW sibling screen: QUOTATION COMPARISON for ProcureAI. The input image is the visual reference and editable base for the app shell. Preserve exactly its ProcureAI cube logo, wordmark, Meridian Works workspace, complete sidebar navigation, AM/Ada Morgan identity, sample-workspace label, header/search/notifications, typography, proportions, restrained forest-green action color, white/cool-off-white light theme, subtle borders and icon style. Keep the same landscape aspect ratio and high resolution. Highlight "Quotations" in the sidebar instead of Overview. Replace only the workspace's actual page content, do not reuse overview cards. Full-bleed flat product screenshot, no device frame or design annotations. All content sharp, correctly spelled, thoughtfully aligned, fully within the viewport.

MAIN PAGE:
Top breadcrumb in header "Workspace / Quotations / Compare". At top of content a small back link "All quotations". Header "Compare quotations" in the same 28px hierarchy; subheading "PR-014 · 20 development laptops". Right buttons outlined "Export comparison" and solid forest-green "Prepare award review". Just below a compact requirement strip separated by fine horizontal rules, containing "Quantity 20 laptops", "Budget $20,000 · total quoted cost", "Required by 8 Dec 2026", "Currency USD".
Two tabs, "Commercial comparison" selected and "Specification match". Main content is one large precise supplier comparison matrix, NOT a repetitive floating-card grid. Four columns: left row labels about 25%, then equal supplier columns for Atlas Computing, Vertex Technologies, Northline Systems. In header each supplier with a simple letter monogram, quote ID Q-014-A/B/C and "Revision 2" for Atlas / "Revision 1" for the others. Atlas header gets subtle pale green tint and a small quiet text check "Lowest eligible total"; Vertex a restrained amber text/icon "Delivery does not meet deadline"; Northline neutral check "Eligible".
Rows:
"Unit price" | "$850.00" | "$790.00" | "$880.00".
"Quantity" | "20" | "20" | "20".
"Item subtotal" | "$17,000.00" | "$15,800.00" | "$17,600.00".
"Freight" | "$300.00" | "$200.00" | "$200.00".
"Quoted tax" | "$1,000.00" | "$900.00" | "$1,000.00".
"Total quoted cost" heavier type, light tinted row | "$18,300.00" | "$16,900.00" | "$18,800.00".
"Delivery" | "12 days · 5 Dec" | "21 days · 14 Dec" amber | "10 days · 3 Dec".
"Warranty" | "24 months" | "12 months" | "36 months".
"Payment terms" | "Net 30" | "Net 15" | "Net 30".
"Mandatory specifications" | "Meets requirements" | "Meets requirements" | "Meets requirements".
"Source quotation" | underlined "Atlas quote · p. 1–2" | "Vertex quote · p. 1–2" | "Northline quote · p. 1–2" with tiny document icons.
Each supplier header includes a small "View source" text action. Use fine row/column separators, tabular numeric alignment and comfortable row height. No green blanket score or star ratings.
Below matrix, a two-part functional recommendation strip: left small restrained line icon and heading "Recommended: Atlas Computing"; body "Lowest total among offers meeting the specification and delivery deadline. Vertex is less expensive but arrives after the required date." Right "Budget headroom" "$1,700" with secondary "Not a savings claim". Under a thin divider a compact evidence line "Critical fields reviewed · 3 supplier quotations · Comparison version 3", plus a contextual "Ask copilot about this comparison" action.
Visible footer note "Illustrative supplier quotes · USD amounts include quoted freight and tax". Do not introduce invoices, payments, subscription plans, charts or supplier risk scores. This is a practical comparison screen with traceable facts, not a generic AI dashboard.

screens.title: Supplier award approval review
screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the reference application screenshot into a NEW sibling screen: SUPPLIER AWARD APPROVAL REVIEW for ProcureAI. The input image is the visual reference and editable base for the app shell. Preserve exactly its ProcureAI cube logo/wordmark, Meridian Works selector, complete left navigation, Ada Morgan / AM identity, sample-workspace label, header/search/notifications, spacing, sharp typography, proportions, white and cool-off-white theme, restrained forest-green, small radii, subtle borders and unified line icons. Same landscape aspect ratio, same high-resolution crisp finish. Highlight "Approvals" with its count 2 instead of Overview. Replace workspace content with an intentional decision workspace, not overview cards. No outside browser/device frame or explanatory artboard labels.

HEADER: top breadcrumb "Workspace / Approvals / PR-014". Small back link "Approval inbox". Title "Review supplier award", secondary "PR-014 · 20 development laptops". Right understated "View request" action. Immediately below a short horizontal process indicator "1 Supplier award" active, fine connector, "2 PO release" neutral; not a flashy graphic.

LAYOUT:
Wide main reading column about 68%, narrower right decision column about 32%, with generous alignment and fine separators rather than rounded floating cards.
In reading column, heading "Award recommendation", then supplier name "Atlas Computing", secondary "Approved supplier · Quote Q-014-A, revision 2". Under this a well-proportioned 3-column inline summary: "Total quoted cost $18,300", "Delivery 5 Dec 2026", "Budget headroom $1,700".
Section "What you are approving" with quiet two-column definition list:
"Requested by" "Daniel Okafor · Engineering";
"Quantity" "20 laptops";
"Required specification" "Core i7 · 16 GB RAM · 512 GB SSD";
"Required by" "8 Dec 2026";
"Payment terms" "Net 30";
"Warranty" "24 months".
Section "Decision basis" with three concise check-icon lines: "Meets all mandatory specifications"; "Delivery is within the required deadline"; "Lowest total among eligible quotations".
Section "Alternatives considered", compact precise table: "Supplier | Total | Outcome"; "Vertex Technologies | $16,900 | Excluded: 21-day delivery"; "Northline Systems | $18,800 | Eligible: faster delivery". Neutral and restrained amber status text.
Section "Supporting evidence", two document rows each with a small line document icon, filename, metadata, and text link: "Atlas quotation.pdf" "Revision 2 · pages 1–2" "View source"; "Quotation comparison" "Version 3 · 3 offers" "Open comparison".
Small "Approval history" timeline beneath: "23 Nov, 14:10 · Daniel Okafor submitted award for review" and "23 Nov, 14:12 · Critical quotation fields confirmed". All dates and texts readable.

RIGHT DECISION SECTION:
Heading "Your decision". A subtle pale neutral/green strip with shield/check icon and text "You are an assigned approver", secondary "Ada Morgan · Authority up to $25,000".
Definition list with fine rules: "Review type Supplier award"; "Packet version 3"; "Request cap $20,000"; "Exceptions None".
Labeled multiline field "Decision note (optional)" with actual quiet example "Add a note for the purchasing team..." in empty-state muted text, not a prefilled approval.
Unchecked square checkbox labeled "I have reviewed the quotation and commercial terms." Make it a clear prerequisite, and render the primary action initially disabled in a muted but legible green-gray to represent required confirmation.
Full-width button "Approve supplier award" with a lock/check icon, visibly disabled pending the checkbox. Beneath two outlined secondary actions side-by-side "Request changes" and "Reject".
A clear short note: "This approves the supplier selection. The purchase order requires a separate release review." This is meaningful product governance, not implementation jargon.
At bottom a small pale neutral context section "Need more context?" with "Review the comparison or ask the procurement copilot." and a quiet "Open copilot" button.
No implication that AI can approve; no payment/send/issue button; no subscriptions, no scores or fake charts. Faithfully render one practical, evidence-driven human approval screen with accessible contrast and precision.
